claims.statement: Covered batteries placed on the market or put into service from 18 February 2027 require a battery passport; this does not create passports for legacy installed batteries.

Passport data can support residual-value and routing decisions, but individual health and history data are restricted to legitimate-interest purposes and commercially sensitive access must be minimized.
The Commission's current page places the battery access-rights implementing act in Q4 2026, so the exact user classes and download, sharing and reuse rights remain unsettled at the access date.
The DPP registry now expressly covers batteries, but registry operation does not itself grant this proposed broker access to restricted battery data.
A defensible non-waste or end-of-waste route requires testing, further-use documentation and protected transport; absence of required proof can cause a shipment to be treated as waste or illegal.
Free producer or producer-responsibility take-back for waste industrial and EV batteries invalidates the original owner-paid waste-routing assumption.
Polish operations should verify partner authorization in BDO and leave ADR transport to qualified carriers; current enforcement shows documentation failures are material.

The strongest economic contrary evidence is that second-life battery reuse remains difficult and early because of safety, warranty, uncertain remaining life, falling new-battery prices, repurposing costs and transferred liability.

Cling and Circunomics directly compete on assessment, condition data, buyer matching, transaction documentation and logistics, so a Polish entrant needs real installer notice rights rather than a generic marketplace.
Poland's storage fleet is expanding, but the reviewed installation figures do not establish near-term commercial retirement counts or sellable condition.
No reviewed source verifies installer willingness to grant first-notice rights, transaction prices, testing cost, buyer acceptance rates, brokerage margins or insurance availability for this entrant.

contrary_evidence: The statutory free producer/EPR waste take-back route removes the proposed owner fee for simple compliant disposal.
Legacy batteries and early retirement events may have no passport, and restricted-data access rules are not yet final.
IEA evidence says second-life reuse is still economically and operationally difficult and used-battery flows remain early.
Established European incumbents already offer the same assessment, transaction and logistics bundle.
Poland's growing storage count reflects recent installations, not immediate feedstock.
A single classification, packaging or ADR error can turn a transaction into a high-liability event.
